summary: A TypeScript library that wraps Playwright's Page with self-healing selector logic. When a primary selector times out, a scoring engine parses the live DOM with cheerio, scores every candidate node against a stored semantic fingerprint (visible text, label associations, ARIA, sibling context, classes, id), and rewrites the locator on the fly. Verified from source: SmartPage.ts orchestrates capture-heal-retry with a flow of store.resolvePrimary.attemptHeal using SelfHealingEngine.ts, which implements a six-signal weighted heuristic producing both CSS and XPath fallback selectors. The library is zero LLM, offline, deterministic.

findings.description: 1. Heavyweight DOM fingerprinting: SmartPage.captureMetadata() runs locator.evaluate() to harvest tag, id, every class, every attribute, innerText, parentText (own text nodes only), siblingTexts, label text (by for= attribute or DOM nesting), aria-label, role, data-testid, and URL pathname. 2. Six-signal weighted heuristic (visible text 0.45, anchor context 0.20, tag 0.10, attributes 0.10, classes 0.10, id 0.05) with configurable weights and threshold. Anchor sub-score itself has inner 5-factor blend (label 0.40, parentText 0.20, aria 0.15, testid 0.10, siblings 0.15). 3. Dual selector output: CSS (preferring data-testid/data-test/id/aria-label/name/classes) and XPath with normalize-space() for button/link/label text matching. CSS-first with XPath fallback at retry time. 4. Re-capture on heal: fingerprint is refreshed from healed node's current DOM so each mutation scores against fresh data. 5. Healing audit trail: stores rolling list of healedFrom selectors (last 10) per logical element. 6. Configurable captureMode: auto vs readonly. 7. SelfHealingEngine is Playwright-free — accepts raw HTML string, unit-testable in isolation. 8. IMetadataStore interface with JSON file backend, swappable to SQLite/Redis. 9. StateReporter produces console summary and JSON artifact on disk.

apiSurface: Users create SmartPage wrapping a Playwright Page via SmartPage constructor passing store, engine, and status reporter. Page Object pattern: CheckoutPage stores logical element constants, then calls agent.smart.fill(logicalName, value, selectorHint) or agent.smart.click(logicalName, selectorHint). LogicalName is static identifier key (e.g. 'checkout.submitButton'). SelectorHint is a default selector used only when store has no prior entry. SmartPage.expectVisible() for assertion, and smart.text() for text extraction. Raw Playwright Page exposed as agent.smart.raw for escape-hatch assertions. The Page Object code never changes post-seed — all drifts heal automatically.
integrationPoints: 1. Replace JSON storage with a Redis or Postgres store via IMetadataStore's 5-method consideration for shared pipeline memory of elements fingerprint. 2. SelfHealingEngine.heal() is environment-free and could be extracted into an API microservice (Node.js or compiled to Wasm) for rapid stateless scoring. 3. Semantic fingerprint model (by label, anchor context, parent text, siblings) is directly usable as Veridian element descriptor format for cross-page-repeat matching. 4. Dual CSS/XPath output with runtime fallback retry directly maps to a robust deterministic scraper outriggers. 5. Per-signal breakdown in HealCandidate could feed into Veridian's confidence scoring, flagging low-confidence matches for manual review rather than silent false positive extraction.
strengthsForVeridian: 1. Deterministic healing, zero LLM — fits any privacy-sensitive scraping pipe. 2. Stateless engine takes raw HTML + struct — trivially embeddable in any pipeline stage. 3. Semantic fingerprinting captures label, parent, siblings, aria — the exact signals a reconnaance-scraper needs to rematch elements across updates. 4. Tunable weights and thresholds enable per-domain optimization for product grids vs. product detail pages vs. checkout flows. 5. SOLID interface decomposition means no component lock-in. 6. TypeScript strict mode, well-typed — strong guarantee for pipeline data operations.
weaknessesForVeridian: 1. Single commit solo prototype — zero adoption evidence, if problems emerge the user is alone. 2. No Shadow DOM/Web Component support — cheerio parses only the flat page.content() tree. 3. Metadata store is local JSON only — multi-instance pipeline workers have no shared decision store. 4. Blind threshold acceptance with no multi-candidate strategy — a high-scoring false positive on architecturally similar but economically different element pairs (two product cards, two submit buttons on same page) catastrophically degrades scraping correctness. 5. String similarity (Levenshtein, Jaccard) breaks when elements shift semantically (text-to-icon, full redesign) — Phase 5 embedding plan not built. 6. CSS/XPath fallback is blind retry, creates no feedback for preference re-evaluation. 7. No data extraction concept — the library strictly handles interactions (click, fill), not scraping of structured content.
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
